evals.name: single-video-compile
evals.prompt: Compile this talk into a detailed reference article: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qp0HIF3SfI4 (Simon Sinek, How Great Leaders Inspire Action)
evals.expected_output: A raw transcript file under raw/youtube/ plus a compiled markdown article (in notes/ or wiki/) with an embedded player, named content sections, clickable timestamps, and direct quotes.
expectations: The fetch was run as `uv run scripts/youtube_fetch.py <url>` and a raw file was written to raw/youtube/ with frontmatter containing title, channel, video_id, and the full transcript
A compiled article was written containing an iframe embed pointing at https://www.youtube.com/embed/qp0HIF3SfI4
The article has at least 3 sections named after the video's actual content, not generic names like 'Part 1' or 'Section 2'
The article contains clickable timestamps of the form [MM:SS](https://youtu.be/qp0HIF3SfI4?t=NNN)
The article contains at least one direct quote attributed to the speaker with a timestamp
Every factual claim in the article can be traced back to text present in the raw transcript file; nothing was fabricated

evals.name: playlist-course-compile
evals.prompt: Process this course playlist into notes: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLZHQObOWTQDNU6R1_67000Dx_ZCJB-3pi
evals.expected_output: Per-video raw files under raw/youtube/, a playlist index file, and a course overview article with a videoseries embed, curriculum table, and topic clusters.
expectations: A playlist index markdown file ending in -playlist.md was written to raw/youtube/ containing the playlist title, channel, and a list of the videos
Individual raw files were written to raw/youtube/ for the playlist's videos, each with a two-digit numeric prefix and its transcript
A course overview article was written containing an iframe whose src includes videoseries?list=PLZHQObOWTQDNU6R1_67000Dx_ZCJB-3pi
The course article's curriculum lists the videos in order with links to their raw files and durations
The skill asked the user before compiling individual lecture articles rather than writing them all silently

evals.name: no-transcript-handling
evals.expected_output: A raw metadata file under raw/youtube/ with no transcript, and a compiled article that notes the missing captions without fabricating any transcript content.
expectations: A raw file was written to raw/youtube/ whose word_count is 0 (no transcript was invented)
The raw file explicitly indicates that no transcript/captions are available for the video
The compiled article explicitly notes that the video has no captions or transcript
The compiled article contains no quotes or timestamp links sourced from a transcript (none exist for this video)

evals.name: non-youtube-url-rejected
evals.expected_output: The skill refuses the non-YouTube URL, clearly reports that only YouTube URLs are accepted, and writes no files.
expectations: The skill reported that the URL is not a valid YouTube URL (e.g. 'Only YouTube URLs are allowed')
The skill did not invoke yt-dlp or youtube-transcript-api against the URL, and wrote no output files
No article or raw file was created for this request
The skill did not fabricate any content from the URL
